chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who applies dye (henna) should not copulate.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why should the one who applies dye not copulate?' He said: 'Because he is restricted (by the dye layer).'

key_terms.مُحْتَصَرٌ: restricted / covered by a barrier layer
key_terms.يُجَامِعُ: to copulate / engage in sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: Why does a person with henna on their hands need to remove it before sexual intercourse or ritual purity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a person with applied dye (mustakhrid) is considered 'muhtasar' (enclosed/barriered), thereby invalidating sexual intercourse until the barrier is removed. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical integrity of the skin for valid ritual purity (taharah), ensuring that water reaches the body during ghusl or wudu without obstruction from substances like henna or paint.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhsayn Bin Ahmad, from Aban, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The dyed one should not copulate’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Why shouldn’t the dyed one copulate?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because he is restricted (by the application of the dye)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Beware of speaking when two sexual organs meet; it may cause dumbness and muteness.’”
